name: Ondo OUSG
oneLiner: OUSG is Ondo's tokenized U.S. T-Bill fund backed mainly by BlackRock BUIDL; a NAV-accreting share (not $1-pegged) limited to U.S. Qualified Purchasers.
collateral: Primarily BlackRock USD Institutional Digital Liquidity Fund (BUIDL), which holds short-term U.S. Treasury bills, cash, and repurchase agreements; secondary allocations to BlackRock FedFund (TFDXX) and USDC for liquidity; Ondo I LP is the largest single holder of BUIDL; migrated from iShares SHV ETF to BUIDL in March 2024
pegMechanism: NAV-accreting fund share token (not pegged to $1); token price rises daily as Treasury income accrues; instant mint/redemption at daily NAV via OUSGInstantManager against USDC (T+0 settlement via BUIDL on-chain liquidity); token transfers restricted to KYC-verified whitelisted addresses on-chain

proofOfReserves.provider: NAV Consulting, Inc. (fund administrator; daily NAV reports published with up to 3-day lag)

jurisdiction.license: Reg D Rule 506(c); Section 3(c)(7) exemption; restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers

applicabilityBasis.summary: OUSG is a Reg D Rule 506(c) / Section 3(c)(7) tokenized fund share restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers; it is a security (fund interest in Ondo I LP) not a payment stablecoin.

genius.licensingRegulator: SEC Reg D / qualified purchaser context
genius.notes: OUSG is treated as outside GENIUS payment-stablecoin tracking because Ondo presents it as a qualified-access tokenized Treasury fund product. The SEC closed its two-year investigation into Ondo Finance without charges in November 2025, confirming no enforcement action.

references.label: SEC drops Ondo Finance investigation — no charges (Nov 2025)

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved from Pharos stablecoin metadata by the blacklistability resolver; no separate manual override source is attached.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Inferred review retained: OUSG resolves to Yes because existing metadata classifies the asset as centralized and no manual override narrows that status.

mintAuthority.summary: OUSG minting is operated through Ondo's qualified-access subscription/redemption path; official docs list the OUSG token and OUSG_InstantManager, and Ethereum AccessControl reads show contract-admin holders, but Safe/module setup is not verified.

controls.label: OUSG_InstantManager
controls.evidence: Ondo docs list OUSG_InstantManager as the contract investors use to instantly buy or redeem OUSG. RPC `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`/`getRoleMember` on the manager returned admin holder 0x5AE21c99FC5f1584D8Cb09a298CFFd92B5d178eF.

controls.label: OUSG token default-admin holder
controls.evidence: RPC `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`/`getRoleMember` on the OUSG token returned 0xAEd4caF2E535D964165B4392342F71bac77e8367; contract bytecode is present, but Safe threshold/modules/guard were not verified.

review.evidence: Ondo describes OUSG as a qualified-access product with instant mints/redemptions; official contract docs identify the token and InstantManager, and Ethereum RPC reads identify current AccessControl admin holders.
unresolvedQuestions: Verify whether the token and manager admin-holder contracts are Safes, and if so record threshold, signerCount, enabled modules, guard, and observed block.
Verify OUSG-specific minter roles beyond DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE before raising confidence above manual-review.
